claims.statement: The WEEE Directive addresses preparation for re-use, refurbishment, recycling and access to treatment information for electrical and electronic equipment.

EU ecodesign rules for covered local space heaters require availability of specified electronic spare parts and repair information; applicability is product-specific and does not establish equivalent rights for every heat pump or inverter.

contrary_evidence: The cited repairability duties are product-specific, while the intended inventory spans products that may lack mandated parts or repair access.

economics.acquisition_route: Unvalidated: place take-back bins and exchange ordering in installer service workflows, starting with the family company's supplier network.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario, not a forecast: validate 200 cores in year 1, reach 2.5 million PLN annual gross profit by year 4, build 3 million PLN owner equity and retained cash by year 6, and 5 million PLN founder net worth in years 8-11.
economics.founder_time: Unvalidated operating estimate: 2-4 hours per day once physical handling is delegated to a repair and logistics partner.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated: 35%-60% gross margin after collection, testing, repair, warranty reserve and unusable-core losses.
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 12-24 months if enough failures cluster around a manageable set of models.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated commercial figures, including capital_required_pln: 400-2,500 PLN gross profit per exchanged module plus 250-600 PLN monthly priority membership.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Unvalidated: repeat follows installed-base failures and installer service contracts; failure frequency is unknown.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: More cores create deeper inventory; every test and field return improves model-level pricing and quality control
fingerprint.customer: Renewable-energy and HVAC service firms needing fast, lower-cost out-of-warranty repair
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Contractual take-back loop embedded in the same installers that buy replacement modules
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Advance-exchange inventory backed by managed testing, refurbishment and a limited warranty
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The installer pays when a verified exchange unit ships or for priority access
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A field diagnosis identifies a failed replaceable electronic module

founder_fit: Leverages the family installer's service flow.
Operations can be delegated while the founder handles analytics and partner design.
risks: Waste-status mistakes or unsafe repairs create regulatory and product-liability exposure.
OEM part pairing can prevent reuse.
Inventory can fragment across too many models.

structure.commercial_archetype: Circular spare-parts exchange with managed refurbishment
structure.control_point: Installer take-back and first-refusal contracts over failed modules, plus a serialised test, failure and repair-outcome corpus
structure.critical_dependency: Lawful waste handling, qualified repair partners, product safety and access to sufficient model-specific technical information

thesis: Contract renewable and HVAC installers to route failed out-of-warranty inverters, controls and circuit boards into a managed take-back channel; qualified repair partners test or refurbish modules and the network supplies verified advance-exchange parts back to installers. First-refusal supply rights, model-specific failure data and inventory density form the moat.
title: Renewable-Electronics Harvest and Exchange Network
